I'm checking the CA coordinates around residues 669-674 to figure out the secondary structure geometry near S672, since this region appears to be part of a beta-strand-rich domain.

The i to i+2 CA distances all come out around 6-7 Å, consistent with an extended strand conformation rather than a helix. Now I'm trying to identify whether this strand pairs with a neighboring strand by scanning other residues' CA coordinates for close spatial proximity, which would confirm it's part of a beta sheet.

Residues 736 and 737 turn up within roughly 5-6 Å of S672, a distance typical for paired strand backbones, so I'm checking their backbone N and O atom positions to see if the geometry supports actual hydrogen bonding between the strands.

That distance works out to about 2.85 Å, which is a strong hydrogen bond, confirming these strands are pairing at this point. I'm now checking whether there's a reciprocal H-bond nearby to solidify the beta pairing pattern.

Checking S672 N against S737 O gives a distance of about 2.87 Å too, so both bonds line up—this confirms an antiparallel beta strand pairing at this location.
